name: Nikon Z5II

sensor.readout_notes: No measured stills electronic-shutter readout was found. DPReview says readout is faster than the original Z5's but still slow enough that the e-shutter is best avoided except for silent shooting or the JPEG-only bursts, which use a faster 12-bit readout. Photography Life expects it to be about 1/20 s, like the Zf; that is an estimate, not a measurement. Video readout (DPReview): 4K 24/25/30p full width 22.2 ms (17.8 ms with e-VR crop). 4K 50/60p (1.52× crop) 14.6 ms. N-RAW 4K30 22.2 ms at 1.00×, 11.6 ms at 1.52× crop.

iso.extended: Hi 0.3–Hi 1.7 (up to ISO 204800 equivalent). No Lo setting is listed for stills.
iso.ptp_notes: PhotonsToPhotos published Z5II data (Nikon Rumors, 2025-05-07), but the chart is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read here. The dual-gain ISO is unverified.

ibis.notes: 5-axis sensor-shift VR: 7.5 stops at the center and 6.0 stops at the periphery (CIPA 2024, Z 24-120mm f/4 S at telephoto, NORMAL). Focus-point VR (menu label 'Link VR to focus point') centers the correction on the active AF point. It works only in photo mode, only with NIKKOR Z lenses that have no VR, and not when multiple focus points are displayed. Nikon sources fetched here do not mention Synchro VR for the Z5II, so the field is null. Electronic VR for video.

shutter.electronic_fastest: 1/8000 (Nikon lists a single 1/8000–30 s range. A separate electronic-shutter top speed is not stated.)
shutter.flash_sync: 1/200 s or slower. Auto FP high-speed sync up to 1/8000 s. Flash support with the fully electronic shutter was not confirmed.
shutter.slowest: 30 s standard. 900 s in M with extended shutter speeds. Bulb and Time also available.
shutter.notes: Vertical-travel focal-plane mechanical shutter, electronic front-curtain, and electronic shutter (Custom setting d6). With the slow e-shutter readout, use mechanical or EFCS for anything that moves. Pixel shift always uses the electronic shutter.

drive.max_fps_raw: About 11 fps RAW with the mechanical shutter (DPReview). Nikon's C-H (extended) rates are 14 fps (mechanical) and 15 fps (silent). Nikon's footnote limits the high rates to non-RAW image quality. DPReview's press-release notes say 14 fps mechanical is JPEG only.
drive.pre_release_capture: Yes. C15 and C30 (High-Speed Frame Capture+), JPEG only. Buffers up to 1 s before the full press. Options in Custom setting d3.
drive.notes: C-L 1–7 fps. C-H 7.8 fps (mechanical), 9.4 fps (EFCS), 10 fps (silent). 3D-tracking holds at 14 fps.

af.low_light_ev: −10 to +19 EV (f/1.2 lens, ISO 100, 20 °C, AF-S center point). Photography Life standardizes this to −8.5 EV at f/2.
af.notes: 273 points. Nikon says AF takes about one-third the time of the original Z5. AF-A is available. AF/MF subject detection options and an MF subject detection area are in the menus.

ftz_ii_behavior: AF-S, AF-P and AF-I lenses: full AF with electronic rangefinder. Screw-drive AF and AF-D lenses: MF only, with electronic rangefinder. AI-P and non-CPU (AI/AI-S) lenses: MF, modes A and M only. Non-CPU lenses need Non-CPU lens data. Non-VR F lenses get 3-axis IBIS (yaw, pitch, roll). VR F lenses combine lens VR with body roll correction. No Synchro VR. Focus-point VR needs NIKKOR Z lenses, so it is not available on F lenses. Focus shift shooting works with AF-S and AF-P lenses, but auto reset is disabled. Z teleconverters cannot be used on the FTZ II. See accessories/ftz-ii.json.

dx_crop.notes: DX image area L is 3984 × 2656 px, about 10.6 MP (Nikon Asia spec). Only useful for a quick framing crop.

special_features.name: Pixel shift
special_features.notes: About 96 MP from 16 or 32 shots (4 and 8 shots keep 24 MP). Electronic shutter, RAW only, tripod and static subject, merged in NX Studio (DPReview, J.M. Peltier).

special_features.name: Focus shift shooting
special_features.notes: Photo shooting menu (Z5II manual TOC; Photography Life).

special_features.name: Auto capture
special_features.notes: Not in the Z5II Reference Guide TOC.

special_features.name: Bird detection
special_features.notes: Nikon press material: bird detection mode for birds in motion and in flight.

special_features.name: Starlight View
special_features.notes: Custom setting d11 (photo Lv). Warm color display mode is also available.

special_features.name: High-frequency flicker reduction
special_features.notes: In the Photo and Video menus (Z5II manual TOC).

special_features.name: MF subject detection
special_features.notes: MF Subject Detection Area and AF/MF Subject Detection Options are in the TOC. Whether chipped F lenses work is not confirmed by Nikon. J.M. Peltier reports MF detection working with CPU and non-CPU F lenses on the Zf/Z6III (likely, unverified on the Z5II).

special_features.name: Focus-point VR
special_features.notes: Non-VR NIKKOR Z lenses only, photo mode only.

special_features.name: Imaging Recipes (formerly Cloud Picture Control)
special_features.notes: Downloaded through Nikon Imaging Cloud and applied with the dedicated Picture Control button. 31 built-in presets.

special_features.name: Flexible Color Picture Control
special_features.notes: Created in NX Studio and imported as a Custom Picture Control.

special_features.name: Hi-Res Zoom
special_features.notes: Video only: up to 2× at 1080p 24/25/30, FX area.

special_features.name: Focus limiter
special_features.notes: Not in the Z5II manual TOC.

video_key.internal_raw: N-RAW 12-bit to SD: 4032 × 2268 (FX) at 30/25/24p. V90 cards recommended.
video_key.log: N-Log (ISO Lo 0.3–2.0 and 800–51200 in N-Log) and HLG.
video_key.notes: 4K/30 full width. 4K/60 with a 1.5× crop. 1080p to 120p. 10-bit H.265. Electronic VR is not available with N-RAW.

firmware.notable_changes: 1.20 (2026-08-18): 'Cloud Picture Control' renamed 'Imaging Recipe'. Auto ISO minimum shutter speed range updated. 'On saving user settings' option for Save focus position. Automatic monitor display switch. Wi-Fi Always On. FTP inactive timeout. Aperture no longer restricted in S mode video. Bug fixes. 1.11 (May 2026): changes aperture behavior when the standby timer expires. 1.10 (Dec 2025): HDMI output no longer interrupted when recording ends. 1.02 (Nov 2025): sensor cleaning default set to 'Clean at shutdown'. 1.01 (Jun 2025): text and naming changes.

battery_media: EN-EL15c (EN-EL15b/a also fit, with fewer shots). CIPA 330 shots (LCD) per DPReview. MB-N14 grip available. Two SD UHS-II slots.
field_tips: Use the mechanical shutter or EFCS for anything that moves. The non-stacked sensor's electronic shutter reads out slowly and will skew motion.
Pre-release capture (C15/C30) only records JPEG. Switch image quality to JPEG before a bird-takeoff session, or stay on 11 fps RAW mechanical.
Focus-point VR works only with non-VR NIKKOR Z lenses (for example the 26, 28, 40 and 50 primes), in photo mode, with a single focus point. It does nothing for VR lenses or F glass.
For about 96 MP pixel shift, use 16 or 32 shots on a tripod with a still subject, then merge in NX Studio. It always uses the electronic shutter, so watch for flicker under artificial light.
Under LED or venue lighting, enable High-Frequency Flicker Reduction, especially with the electronic shutter.
Since FW 1.02 the default is 'Clean at shutdown'. Leave it on, because the sensor is exposed during lens changes.

research_notes: Pixel pitch = 35.9 / 6048 × 1000 = 5.936, rounded to 5.94 µm (matches Photography Life's 5.94). The stills e-shutter readout is unmeasured: no Kasson, Horshack or PtP figure was found, so the field is null. The ISO range conflicts: Nikon Asia lists 100–51200 in one row and 'highest standard 64000' in another. DPReview and the press release say 100–64000, which is used here. Photography Life lists extended ISO 50, but Nikon lists no Lo for stills. The RAW frame rate is ambiguous: Nikon's footnote and DPReview indicate RAW tops out at about 11 fps mechanical; whether C-H extended at 14/15 fps accepts RAW is unclear. Synchro VR is not mentioned in any Z5II source fetched, so the field is null. The dual-gain ISO is unknown because the PtP chart could not be read. Whether the mechanical shutter closes at power-off is not stated (the TOC has no sensor-shield item). The web search budget ran out before these gaps could be closed.
